title: Meeting the Neighbors
goal: Introduce yourself as a neighbor, respond to an invitation, and exchange a useful local question.

runs.text: I've just moved in next door
explains why you are introducing yourself.
I live upstairs
or
I'm in apartment six
locates your home. A
neighbor
lives nearby; a
housewarming
is a gathering to mark a new home.

turns.speaker: New neighbor

runs.text: Hi, I'm Tessa. I've just moved in next door.

turns.en: Hi, I'm Tessa. I've just moved in next door.

turns.speaker: Neighbor

runs.text: Nice to meet you. I'm Ben. Welcome to the neighborhood.

turns.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Ben. Welcome to the neighborhood.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Thanks. I wanted to introduce myself.

turns.en: Thanks. I wanted to introduce myself.

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: How's the move going?

turns.en: How's the move going?

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Pretty well. We still have a lot to unpack.

turns.en: Pretty well. We still have a lot to unpack.

runs.text: The greeting and name exchange reuse Chapters 1–2. The new information is your relationship as a neighbor and a shared local context.
I just came by to say hello
gives a reason for a brief visit. If the timing is inconvenient:
I don't want to keep you. I'll see you around
closes without forcing a longer conversation.

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: We're having a small housewarming on Saturday. Would you like to come?

turns.en: We're having a small housewarming on Saturday. Would you like to come?

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Thanks. What time?

turns.en: Thanks. What time?

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: Around six.

turns.en: Around six.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: I'd like to, but I'm not sure whether I'll be free. Could I let you know tomorrow?

turns.en: I'd like to, but I'm not sure whether I'll be free. Could I let you know tomorrow?

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: Of course.

turns.en: Of course.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Great. Thanks for asking.

turns.en: Great. Thanks for asking.

runs.text: Around six
is an approximate time.
I'd love to come
accepts with enthusiasm;
I can't make it, but thanks for inviting me
declines.
Maybe
or
I'll let you know
leaves the plan unconfirmed. If you want a brief meeting instead:
Would you like to come over for coffee sometime?
suggests it without fixing a date.
You can set a boundary:
Thanks, but I prefer to keep evenings quiet
or
I won't join this time
. A reason can help, but you do not need to invent one.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Do you know a plumber who works in this area?

turns.en: Do you know a plumber who works in this area?

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: I know someone I've used before. I can send you the business details.

turns.en: I know someone I've used before. I can send you the business details.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: That would help. Thank you.

turns.en: That would help. Thank you.

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: Are you interested in the neighborhood group chat?

turns.en: Are you interested in the neighborhood group chat?

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: What do people use it for?

turns.en: What do people use it for?

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: Mostly local updates and questions.

turns.en: Mostly local updates and questions.

turns.speaker: Tessa

runs.text: Could you tell me how to request an invitation?

turns.en: Could you tell me how to request an invitation?

turns.speaker: Ben

runs.text: Sure.

turns.en: Sure.

blocks.caption: Ask for local information · Tessa & Ben

runs.text: Do you know a...?
asks for a contact or suggestion, not proof that the person is qualified or available.
What is it used for?
checks a group's purpose before joining.
I'd rather not join, but thanks
is a complete decline.
Other questions include
Where can I find the building's information?
Who handles maintenance requests?
, and
Is there a notice board for residents?
When a neighbor does not know:
No problem. I'll ask the manager
keeps the uncertainty visible.

turns.speaker: Neighbor

runs.text: I think this box may be blocking the hallway. Is it yours?

turns.en: I think this box may be blocking the hallway. Is it yours?

turns.speaker: Resident

runs.text: Yes. I didn't realize it was in the way. I'll move it.

turns.en: Yes. I didn't realize it was in the way. I'll move it.

turns.speaker: Neighbor

runs.text: Thanks.

turns.en: Thanks.

turns.speaker: Resident

runs.text: Thanks for letting me know.

turns.en: Thanks for letting me know.

blocks.caption: A minor shared-space concern · Ben & Resident

runs.text: Is it yours?
checks responsibility rather than assuming.
It's in the way
explains the practical concern. You can also say
I'm not sure whose it is. Let's ask before moving it
when ownership is unknown.
Read the other neighbor's turns and answer, then switch roles if alone.
Introduce yourself as the person who moved into apartment 6. Give a short moving update.
A Saturday invitation is offered. Ask the time, then accept, decline, or say you will confirm tomorrow.
Ask about a local repair contact. The neighbor offers a group chat instead; ask what it is for before deciding.
A neighbor asks whether a hallway box is yours. It is not yours and you do not know who owns it. Respond without accusing another person.
Sample possibilities:

“Hi, I'm Tessa. I've moved into apartment six. We're still unpacking.” / “What time? I'd like to come, but could I confirm tomorrow?” / “What is the group chat used for?” / “It isn't mine. I'm not sure whose it is.”
Repeat later with another invitation or local question. Check that the other person could distinguish your introduction, confirmed plans and unanswered questions.

ja: 近所で、紹介と小さな相談。
note: 歓迎の言葉と、誘いへの返事を交わします。共有スペースの問題は、責める前に物と状況を特定します。
